paragraphs.text: Global IM channels for DeepSeek Harness — Telegram, Discord, Slack, Mattermost, Zulip and Matrix in
one plugin, with per-conversation sessions that survive restarts.
# dsh-im-global
[](https://github.com/monkey-sking/dsh-im-global/blob/main/LICENSE) [](https://github.com/monkey-ski
ng/dsh-im-global/commits/main) [](https://github.com/monkey-sking/dsh-im-global/search?l=JavaScript)
[](https://github.com/monkey-sking/dsh-im-global/stargazers) [](https://github.com/monkey-sking/dsh
-im-global/network/members)
**Global IM channels for DeepSeek Harness** — Telegram, Discord, Slack, Mattermost, Zulip and Matrix
in one plugin, with per-conversation sessions that survive restarts.

> ⚠️ **Security: closed by default.** A channel with no allowlist configured
> rejects every message

(fail-closed) and shows as locked until you add the
> sender's user ids. See Security: the allowlis

t is fail-closed
> before connecting a bot.

It shares its shape with the DingTalk / QQ / WeChat / Feishu / WeCom gateway
(`@lijian-ui/dsh-im-gat

eway`):
one plugin, a `channels: [...]` list, one adapter per platform.
## Why this exists

`dsh-telegram` proved the model but is a single-platform channel owned by a
third party: a single ha

rd-coded language, one platform per package, and no way
to add a second one without a second copy of
the same session plumbing.
This package factors that plumbing out:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Adding a platform is one adapter file. Nothing in `core/` changes.
## Platforms
| type | inbound | needs a public URL? | credentials |

| `telegram` | Bot API long polling | no | bot token (`@BotFather`) |
| `discord` | Gateway WebSocke

t | no | bot token |
| `slack` | Socket Mode WebSocket | no | bot token `xoxb-…` + app token `xapp-…

` |
| `matrix` | `/sync` long polling | no | access token (+ homeserver URL) |
| `mattermost` | WebS

ocket + REST | no | personal access token + base URL |
| `zulip` | event-queue long polling | no | `
<bot email>:<api key>` + base URL |

WhatsApp / Teams / LINE / Messenger are **not** covered: they only deliver events
to a public HTTPS

callback, which is a different hosting shape rather than
another adapter.
## Install
### From the plugin market
Add this index under **Plugins → Discover → Manage index sources**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### From a local checkout
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The bundle inserts one row, `im-global`, into the profile composition.
## Configure (two ways)
### Settings page (no YAML, no restart)

Enable the bundle once, then open **Settings → Chat channels**. The page manages the
channel list: a

dd/remove a channel, pick its type, name the credential, set the
server URL, **test** the credential

against the platform, and save. Saving
restarts the affected channels in place — the process is not

e platform, and save. Saving
restarts the affected channels in place — the process is not restarted.

Credentials are never edited there. The page only stores the credential *name*;
the secret stays in
the credential store.
#### Saving a token directly (builds without a credentials page)

Each channel card also has a **Token（可选，直接保存）** field. Paste the token and
press **保存 token** — the

plugin writes it to `~/.dsh/dsh-im-global/secrets.json`
(mode 0600) and resolves it as a fallback af

ter `ctx.credentials` and the
environment variable of the same name. Useful when the host has no cre

dentials UI:
the channel then starts without touching the host credential store.
### `cordis.patch.yml`

`## Configure` below documents the file-based route, which stays the floor: a
value pinned there is

used until the settings page saves a channel list of its
own.
## Configure

Tokens live in `ctx.credentials`, never in the config file. Create them first —
via the credentials

settings page or the host's credential store — under the
names the channel references:
| platform | default credential | what to paste |

| Telegram | `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | BotFather → `/newbot` → the token it prints |
| Discord | `DISCO

RD_BOT_TOKEN` | Bot → Token (Developer Portal → Bot → Reset Token) |
| Slack | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | O

Auth & Permissions → Bot User OAuth Token (`xoxb-…`) |
| Slack | `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` | Basic Informati

on → App-Level Tokens (`xapp-…`, scope `connections:write`) |
| Matrix | `MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN` | any

account's access token |
| Mattermost | `MATTERMOST_TOKEN` | Profile → Security → Personal Access T

okens |
| Zulip | `ZULIP_BOT_TOKEN` | `<bot email>:<api key>` from Settings → Bots |
Then edit the `im-global` row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Settings storage

The page writes `~/.dsh/dsh-im-global/settings.json` (atomic temp-file + rename).
When that file exi

sts its `channels` list wins over the composition's; delete it
to fall back to `cordis.patch.yml`.
### Security: the allowlist is fail-closed

A chat bridge turns anyone who can reach the bot into an agent driver, so this
plugin is **closed by

default**. A channel with no allowlist configured accepts
nothing — not even the owner — and shows

as **locked** on the Settings page with
every inbound message dropped and logged.

To open a channel, put the sender's platform user ids on the list, either in the
Settings page (**允许
的用户 id** field, comma separated) or in the composition:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A per-channel `allowedUsers` wins; otherwise the plugin-level `allowedUsers`
applies; if neither is

set the channel stays locked. How to find a user id:
Telegram = the numeric id a bot sees, Discord =

the numeric snowflake, Slack =
the member id, Matrix = the full `@user:server`, Mattermost/Zulip =

the numeric
user id. The bot reads them from the `userId` it logs per inbound message.

This is the *only* gate between the platform and your agent. Treat it like a
firewall rule: configur

e it before exposing a bot, and keep it populated as you
add users.
The gate covers **both** ways a chat can drive the agent:

- a typed message, checked in the router before any session work;
- a **button press** answering a p

ending question, checked in the adapter before
the choice is emitted. A press from an off-list sende

r is refused with
"你不在允许名单上，无法回答" and never reaches the question broker — otherwise
anyone in a grou
p could answer for the owner just by seeing the keyboard.
